---
title: "Transcriptome Analysis"
subtitle: "RNA-seq, differential gene expression"

params:
  # folder with the inputs below; relative paths are resolved against it
  data_dir: "analysis/"
  dds: "deseq2/dds.Rds"
  results_dir: "deseq2/results"
  summary: "deseq2/results/dds_summary.tsv"
  annotation: "annotation/ensembl_human_v115.tsv"
  enrichment_dir: "analysis/pathway_enrichment"
  # adjusted p-value cut-off; 0 = use the alpha from DESEQ2_RESULTS
  alpha: 0
  lfc: 0
  export_fig: false
---

```{r import-datasets}
# Local preview, with the published DESeq2 outputs in one folder:
# quarto preview transcriptome_report.qmd -P data_dir:<outdir>/deseq2
resolve <- function(x) {
  if (file.exists(x)) x else file.path(params$data_dir, x)
}

dds <- readRDS(resolve(params$dds))
summ <- read.delim(resolve(params$summary))

# Variable of interest: the last column of the design, as in DESEQ2_RESULTS
group_var <- tail(all.vars(design(dds)), 1)
lvls <- levels(dds[[group_var]])
ref <- lvls[1]
contrasts <- lvls[-1]

# One DESEQ2_RESULTS table per contrast: <prefix>_<level>_vs_<ref>.tsv
read_results <- function(contrast, dir) {
  files <- list.files(dir, pattern = "_vs_.*\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
  file <- files[endsWith(files, paste0("_", contrast, "_vs_", ref, ".tsv"))]
  if (length(file) != 1) {
    stop(
      "Expected 1 results table for ", contrast, " vs ", ref, ", found ",
      length(file), " in: ", dir
    )
  }

  tbl <- read.delim(file)
  data.frame(
    gene_id = tbl$gene_id,
    contrast = contrast,
    log2fc = tbl$log2FoldChange,
    log2fc_shrunk = tbl$log2FoldChange_shrunk,
    padj = tbl$padj
  )
}

res <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(contrasts, read_results, dir = resolve(params$results_dir))
)

if (params$annotation != "") {
  path <- resolve(params$annotation)
  sep <- if (grepl("\\.csv(\\.gz)?$", path)) "," else "\t"
  anno <- read.delim(path, sep = sep)
  anno <- anno[!duplicated(anno$gene_id), ]
}

# pathway_enrichment_ora.R and pathway_enrichment_gsea.R: one Rds per
# contrast and method, list(terms, stats, universe, settings)
enr_dir <- resolve(params$enrichment_dir)
enr_files <- list.files(enr_dir, pattern = "\\.Rds$", full.names = TRUE)

ora_files <- grep("_ora\\.Rds$", enr_files, value = TRUE)
gsea_files <- grep("_gsea\\.Rds$", enr_files, value = TRUE)

if (length(ora_files) == 0) {
  stop("No ORA Rds files (*_ora.Rds) in: ", enr_dir)
}

other <- setdiff(enr_files, c(ora_files, gsea_files))
if (length(other) > 0) {
  warning(
    "Ignored Rds files that are neither *_ora.Rds nor *_gsea.Rds: ",
    toString(basename(other))
  )
}

# Read one method's Rds files and check their layout
read_enrichment <- function(files) {
  enr <- lapply(files, readRDS)
  is_enr <- vapply(enr, function(x) {
    is.list(x) &&
      all(c("terms", "stats", "universe", "settings") %in% names(x))
  }, logical(1))
  if (!all(is_enr)) {
    stop(
      "Not an enrichment Rds with terms, stats, universe and settings: ",
      toString(basename(files[!is_enr]))
    )
  }
  enr
}

enr <- read_enrichment(ora_files)
gsea <- read_enrichment(gsea_files)
has_gsea <- length(gsea) > 0

# Enrichment contrast -> DESeq2 level: "DDS_summer_2022_vs_control" and
# "summer_2022_vs_control" both give "summer_2022"; the longest level wins
match_level <- function(x) {
  ends_with_level <- vapply(contrasts, function(l) {
    grepl(paste0("(^|_)", l, "_vs_", ref, "$"), x)
  }, logical(1))
  hit <- contrasts[x == contrasts | ends_with_level]
  if (length(hit) == 0) {
    stop(
      "Enrichment contrast '", x, "' matches none of: ",
      toString(contrasts)
    )
  }
  hit[which.max(nchar(hit))]
}

enr_contrasts <- c(enr, gsea) |>
  lapply(function(e) e$universe$contrast) |>
  unlist() |>
  unique()
lvl_map <- setNames(vapply(enr_contrasts, match_level, ""), enr_contrasts)
```

```{r parameters}
# adjusted p-value, the same as in DESEQ2_RESULTS unless set in params
Q_CUT <- if (params$alpha > 0) params$alpha else summ$alpha[1]
LFC <- if (params$lfc > 0) params$lfc else 0

# genes listed in the "shared by all groups" table
TOP_N <- 50

# PCA: number of most variable genes, as in DESeq2::plotPCA() and QUANT_QC
PCA_NTOP <- 500
```

```{r QoL-functions}
has_ann <- function(x) !is.na(x) & nzchar(trimws(as.character(x)))

pct <- function(n, d, digits = 1) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), if (d == 0) 0 else 100 * n / d)
}

# "a", "a and b", "a, b and c"
enum <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) <= 1) return(x)
  paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
}

# "summer_2022" -> "Summer 2022"
label_group <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("_", " ", x)
  paste0(toupper(substr(x, 1, 1)), substring(x, 2))
}
group_lab <- setNames(label_group(lvls), lvls)
lab_fun <- function(x) unname(group_lab[x])

# Gene symbol from the annotation, or the Ensembl ID without one
gene_label <- function(id) {
  if (is.null(anno) || !"gene_name" %in% colnames(anno)) return(id)
  nm <- anno$gene_name[match(id, anno$gene_id)]
  ifelse(has_ann(nm), nm, id)
}

# "1,234 (↑ 600 : ↓ 634)"
fmt_dir <- function(x) {
  paste0(
    comma(length(x)),
    " (↑ ", comma(sum(x == "Up")),
    " : ↓ ", comma(sum(x == "Down")), ")"
  )
}

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Export figures and captions from code chunks, to be included in manuscript
# Extract name, size and other parameters to match the reports design/layout
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Name defaults to the chunk label, size to the chunk's fig-width/fig-height.
fig_opts <- function(name, width, height) {
  list(
    name = name %||% knitr::opts_current$get("label") %||% "figure",
    width = width %||% knitr::opts_current$get("fig.width") %||% 7,
    height = height %||% knitr::opts_current$get("fig.height") %||% 5
  )
}

# Save the chunk's caption (and sub-captions)
save_caption <- function(name) {
  # A caption written as `!expr paste0(...)` comes back as an unevaluated
  # expression, so evaluate it like knitr does for the rendered caption
  as_text <- function(x) {
    if (is.language(x) || is.expression(x)) {
      x <- eval(x, envir = knitr::knit_global())
    }
    if (is.null(x)) NULL else as.character(unlist(x))
  }
  get_opt <- function(x) {
    opt <- knitr::opts_current$get(x) %||%
      knitr::opts_current$get(gsub(".", "-", x, fixed = TRUE))
    as_text(opt)
  }
  cap <- get_opt("fig.cap") %||% get_opt("tbl.cap")
  sub <- get_opt("fig.subcap")
  if (is.null(cap) && is.null(sub)) return(invisible(NULL))

  lines <- c(
    cap,
    if (length(sub)) paste0("(", letters[seq_along(sub)], ") ", sub)
  )
  writeLines(lines, paste0(name, "-caption.txt"))
  invisible(NULL)
}

# for "regular" ggplot objects
save_figure <- function(p, name = NULL, width = NULL, height = NULL) {
  o <- fig_opts(name, width, height)
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = paste0(o$name, ".pdf"),
    plot = p,
    width = o$width,
    height = o$height,
    device = grDevices::cairo_pdf
  )
  save_caption(o$name)
}
```

```{r color-schema}
series_colours <- c(

  if (use_shapes) point_shapes[seq_along(lvls)] else rep(21, length(lvls)),

)
```

```{r significance-tbl}
res$sign <- !is.na(res$padj) & res$padj < Q_CUT
res$direction <- ifelse(res$log2fc > 0, "Up", "Down")
sig <- res[res$sign, ]

# Number of groups each DEG is significant in, and whether the direction is
# the same in all of them
n_groups <- tapply(sig$contrast, sig$gene_id, length)
same_dir <- tapply(sig$direction, sig$gene_id, function(d) {
  length(unique(d)) == 1
})

ids_unique <- names(n_groups)[n_groups == 1]
ids_shared <- names(n_groups)[n_groups >= 2]
ids_all <- names(n_groups)[n_groups == length(contrasts)]
```

```{r number-for-report}
n_genes <- nrow(dds)
n_union <- length(n_groups)
n_shared <- length(ids_shared)
n_shared_same <- sum(same_dir[ids_shared])
n_all <- length(ids_all)
n_all_same <- sum(same_dir[ids_all])

# "1,234 in Summer 2022 (600 up, 634 down)"
count_text <- function(ids = NULL) {
  vapply(contrasts, function(x) {
    s <- sig[sig$contrast == x, ]
    if (!is.null(ids)) s <- s[s$gene_id %in% ids, ]
    sprintf(
      "%s in %s (%s up, %s down)",
      comma(nrow(s)),
      group_lab[[x]],
      comma(sum(s$direction == "Up")),
      comma(sum(s$direction == "Down"))
    )
  }, character(1))
}
```

::: {.callout-note title="Method" collapse=true}

<!-- TODO: describe the experiment: tissue, exposure, sampling per season -->

Gene-level counts were imported from salmon quantifications with tximport and tested for differential expression with DESeq2. Each `r group_var` group was compared with `r ref` using the Wald test, and log~2~ fold changes were shrunk with apeglm. P-values were adjusted for multiple testing with the Benjamini–Hochberg method, and genes with an adjusted p-value < `r Q_CUT` were termed **D**ifferentially **E**xpressed **G**enes (***DEGs***). Counts of DEGs use the unshrunk fold change for the direction, the same as `DDS_summary.tsv`.

# Results

## Sample clustering

```{r pca}
# vst() needs at least 1,000 genes for its subsample
vsd <- if (nrow(dds) >= 1000) {
  vst(dds, blind = TRUE)
} else {
  varianceStabilizingTransformation(dds, blind = TRUE)
}

pca <- plotPCA(
  vsd,
  intgroup = group_var,
  ntop = PCA_NTOP,
  returnData = TRUE
)
pct_var <- 100 * attr(pca, "percentVar")
names(pca)[names(pca) == "name"] <- "sample"
```

The first two principal components of the **`r comma(min(PCA_NTOP, n_genes))`** most variable genes explaining **`r sprintf("%.1f", pct_var[1])` %** and **`r sprintf("%.1f", pct_var[2])` %** of the variance, see @fig-pca.

@fig-sample-dist shows the same samples as distances between every pair, clustered so that the most similar samples sit next to each other. Samples of one group that cluster together share an expression profile. A sample that clusters away from its group, can point to an outlier or a batch effect.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Sample distances

```{r fig-sample-dist}
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Sample-to-sample distances. Euclidean distances between the variance-stabilised counts (vst, blind to the design) of all ", comma(n_genes), " genes (after filtering steps). Samples are ordered by hierarchical clustering (complete linkage), shown by the dendrogram. Darker means more similar; the colour strips show each sample's group.")
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9

# Euclidean distances between samples, as in the DESeq2 vignette
sample_dist <- dist(t(assay(vsd)))
sample_hc <- hclust(sample_dist, method = "complete")
samples <- sample_hc$labels[sample_hc$order]
n_samples <- length(samples)
sample_grp <- setNames(dds[[group_var]], colnames(dds))

# Segments of the dendrogram, with the leaves at x = 1, 2, ... in the
# clustering order, as the columns of the heat map
dendro_segments <- function(hc) {
  n <- length(hc$order)
  leaf_x <- integer(n)
  leaf_x[hc$order] <- seq_len(n)
  node_x <- numeric(n - 1)

  # merge: negative = a leaf, positive = an earlier merge
  pos <- function(i) {
    if (i < 0) c(leaf_x[-i], 0) else c(node_x[i], hc$height[i])
  }

  segs <- lapply(seq_len(n - 1), function(k) {
    a <- pos(hc$merge[k, 1])
    b <- pos(hc$merge[k, 2])
    h <- hc$height[k]
    node_x[k] <<- (a[1] + b[1]) / 2

    data.frame(
      x = c(a[1], b[1], a[1]),
      xend = c(a[1], b[1], b[1]),
      y = c(a[2], b[2], h),
      yend = c(h, h, h)
    )
  })

  do.call(rbind, segs)
}

# Long table of the distance matrix; the first sample of the order at the
# top left
dist_mat <- as.matrix(sample_dist)
dist_df <- data.frame(
  x = factor(rep(colnames(dist_mat), each = nrow(dist_mat)), levels = samples),
  y = factor(
    rep(rownames(dist_mat), times = ncol(dist_mat)),
    levels = rev(samples)
  ),
  dist = as.vector(dist_mat)
)

p_dendro <- ggplot(dendro_segments(sample_hc)) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
    linewidth = 0.4,
    colour = "grey30"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, n_samples + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  theme_void()

strip_df <- data.frame(sample = samples, group = sample_grp[samples])

p_top <- ggplot(
  strip_df,
  aes(factor(sample, levels = samples), 1, fill = group)
) +
  geom_tile(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colours, labels = lab_fun, name = "Groups") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_void(base_size = 13)

p_left <- ggplot(strip_df,
    aes(1, factor(sample, levels = rev(samples)), fill = group)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_void()

p_heat <- ggplot(dist_df, aes(x, y, fill = dist)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  # one-hue sequential ramp: dark = small distance, i.e. similar samples
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#0d366b",
    high = "#eef4fc",
    name = "Distance"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(position = "right", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, colour = "black", size = 10
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", size = 10),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

p <- wrap_plots(
  plot_spacer(), p_dendro,
  plot_spacer(), p_top,
  p_left, p_heat,
  ncol = 2,
  widths = c(0.04, 1),
  heights = c(0.2, 0.04, 1),
  guides = "collect"
)

print(p); if (params$export_fig) save_figure(p)
```

## Descriptive statistics

This section presents numbers without any interpretation of the results. @tbl-summarytable shows the main results.

```{r tbl-summarytable}
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Differentially expressed genes (padj < ", Q_CUT, ", lfc > ", LFC, ") per group, each compared with ", ref, ". ↑ up-regulated, ↓ down-regulated. Tested counts genes with an adjusted p-value, after DESeq2's independent filtering; for Any group it is the number of genes after the gene filter. Unique genes are significant in that group only; shared genes in at least one other group too, in either direction.")

per_group <- lapply(contrasts, function(x) {
  s <- res[res$contrast == x, ]
  d <- s[s$sign, ]
  uniq <- d$gene_id %in% ids_unique

  data.frame(
    Group = group_lab[[x]],
    Tested = comma(sum(!is.na(s$padj))),
    DEGs = fmt_dir(d$direction),
    Unique = fmt_dir(d$direction[uniq]),
    Shared = fmt_dir(d$direction[!uniq])
  )
})

rbind(
  do.call(rbind, per_group),
  data.frame(
    Group = "**Any group**",
    Tested = comma(n_genes),
    DEGs = comma(n_union),
    Unique = comma(length(ids_unique)),
    Shared = comma(n_shared)
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

### Differentially expressed genes

Of the `r comma(n_genes)` tested genes that passed the gene filter, `r enum(count_text())` passed the significance threshold (padj < `r Q_CUT`, lfc > `r LFC`). In total, **`r comma(n_union)` unique DEGs** were found in at least one group.

```{r annot-pie-functions}
# Gene annotation column shown in the pies, e.g. "gene_type" or "chr"
var <- "gene_type"

# Classes with their own colour; the rest are pooled as "other", so every
# slice has a colour and the legend stays short
PIE_MAX_CLASSES <- 6

has_annot_var <- exists("anno") && !is.null(anno) && var %in% names(anno)

# Annotation class per gene; genes missing from the annotation are "unknown"
anno_class <- function(ids, var) {
  strip <- function(x) sub("^(ENS[A-Z]*G[0-9]+)\\.[0-9]+$", "\\1", x)
  cls <- anno[[var]][match(strip(ids), strip(anno$gene_id))]
  ifelse(has_ann(cls), as.character(cls), "unknown")
}

# Significant genes per pie column: one set per group, and the genes in
# common. Common, both directions: significant in every group. Common,
# split: counted once, and only when the direction is the same everywhere
pie_genes <- function() {
  groups <- lapply(contrasts, function(x) {
    sig[sig$contrast == x, c("gene_id", "direction")]
  })
  names(groups) <- unname(group_lab[contrasts])

  same <- ids_all[same_dir[ids_all]]
  com <- sig[sig$gene_id %in% same, c("gene_id", "direction")]

  list(
    groups = groups,
    com_all = data.frame(gene_id = ids_all, direction = rep("Both", n_all)),
    com = com[!duplicated(com$gene_id), ]
  )
}

# Genes per annotation class in one pie column, per direction or combined
build_counts <- function(genes, var, set, by_dir = TRUE) {
  if (nrow(genes) == 0) return(NULL)

  data.frame(
    set = set,
    direction = if (by_dir) genes$direction else "Both",
    class = anno_class(genes$gene_id, var)
  ) |>
    count(set, direction, class, name = "n")
}

# Percentages within each pie, and its total for the "n =" label
prep_pies <- function(d, dir_lvl) {
  d |>
    group_by(set, direction) |>
    mutate(total = sum(n), pct = 100 * n / total) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
      set = factor(set, levels = c(unname(group_lab[contrasts]), "Common")),
      direction = factor(direction, levels = dir_lvl),
      label = ifelse(pct >= 8, sprintf("%.0f%%", pct), "")
    )
}

pie_dir_lab <- c(
  Both = "Both",
  Up = "↑ Up",
  Down = "↓ Down"
)

# One pie per column (set) and row (direction); slices under 8 % unlabelled
plot_pies <- function(d, var, fill_scale) {
  totals <- distinct(d, set, direction, total)

  ggplot(d, aes(x = 1, y = pct, fill = class, group = class)) +
    geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = label),
      position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
      size = 3
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = totals,
      aes(x = 1.62, y = 0, label = paste("n =", comma(total))),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 3.2
    ) +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 1.68)) +
    fill_scale +
    facet_grid(
      direction ~ set,
      drop = FALSE,
      labeller = labeller(direction = pie_dir_lab)
    ) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)),
      panel.spacing = unit(2, "pt")
    )
}

# thin line between (A) and (B)
divider <- ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  theme_void()

# Classes outside `keep` become "other"; counts are summed again
lump_classes <- function(d, keep) {
  d |>
    mutate(class = ifelse(class %in% c(keep, "unknown"), class, "other")) |>
    count(set, direction, class, wt = n, name = "n")
}

# Set2 colours for the kept classes; greys for "other" and "unknown"
pie_colours <- function(lv, palette) {
  keep <- setdiff(lv, c("other", "unknown"))
  cols <- c(
    setNames(scales::brewer_pal(palette = palette)(8)[seq_along(keep)], keep),
    other = "#a6a6a6",
    unknown = "#dcdcdc"
  )
  cols[lv]
}

# full figure: (A) directions combined, (B) split by direction
pie_figure <- function(var, palette = "Set2", name = "Gene type") {
  s <- pie_genes()
  sets <- names(s$groups)

  both <- rbind(
    do.call(rbind, lapply(sets, function(x) {
      build_counts(s$groups[[x]], var, x, by_dir = FALSE)
    })),
    build_counts(s$com_all, var, "Common", by_dir = FALSE)
  )
  split <- rbind(
    do.call(rbind, lapply(sets, function(x) {
      build_counts(s$groups[[x]], var, x)
    })),
    build_counts(s$com, var, "Common")
  )

  # classes from most to fewest genes, "unknown" last, same in A and B
  # the PIE_MAX_CLASSES largest classes over all pies keep their own
  # colour, from most to fewest genes; then "other" and "unknown"
  by_size <- both |>
    count(class, wt = n) |>
    arrange(desc(n)) |>
    pull(class)
  keep <- head(setdiff(by_size, "unknown"), PIE_MAX_CLASSES)
  both <- lump_classes(both, keep)
  split <- lump_classes(split, keep)

  lv <- c(keep, intersect(c("other", "unknown"), c(both$class, split$class)))
  both$class <- factor(both$class, levels = lv)
  split$class <- factor(split$class, levels = lv)

  fill_scale <- scale_fill_manual(
    values = pie_colours(lv, palette),
    name = name,
    drop = FALSE,
    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  )

  both <- prep_pies(both, dir_lvl = "Both")
  split <- prep_pies(split, dir_lvl = c("Up", "Down"))

  p1 <- plot_pies(both, var, fill_scale) +
    theme(strip.text.y = element_blank())
  p2 <- plot_pies(split, var, fill_scale) +
    theme(strip.text.x = element_blank())

  (p1 / divider / p2) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.05, 2), guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = list(c("A", "", "B"))) &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

`r comma(length(ids_unique))` DEGs (`r pct(length(ids_unique), n_union)` %) were significant in one group only: `r enum(count_text(ids_unique))`. `r comma(n_shared)` DEGs (`r pct(n_shared, n_union)` %) were shared by at least two groups, and of these `r comma(n_shared_same)` (`r pct(n_shared_same, n_shared)` %) changed in the same direction in every group they were significant in. `r comma(n_all)` DEGs were significant in all `r length(contrasts)` groups, `r comma(n_all_same)` of them in the same direction (@fig-venn, @tbl-intersections).

```{r venn-functions}
# One set of gene IDs per group, for the given directions
gene_sets <- function(dir = c("Up", "Down")) {
  sets <- lapply(contrasts, function(x) {
    unique(sig$gene_id[sig$contrast == x & sig$direction %in% dir])
  })
  names(sets) <- group_lab[contrasts]
  sets
}

sets_all <- gene_sets()
sets_up <- gene_sets("Up")
sets_down <- gene_sets("Down")

plot_venn <- function(sets, title) {
  if (length(unlist(sets)) == 0) {
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "No genes", size = 5) +
        labs(title = title) +
        theme_void() +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
    )
  }

  ggvenn(
    sets,
    fill_color = unname(group_colours[contrasts]),
    fill_alpha = 0.5,
    stroke_size = 0.6,
    set_name_size = 4.5,
    text_size = 4,
    text_color = "black",
    # 4 sets have 15 regions, too small for a percentage as well
    show_percentage = length(sets) < 4,
    digits = 1
  ) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
}

# Exclusive intersections: each gene counted once, in the exact combination
# of groups it is in, as in the regions of a Venn diagram
all_combos <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(contrasts), function(k) {
  apply(combn(group_lab[contrasts], k), 2, paste, collapse = " & ")
}))

count_combos <- function(sets) {
  ids <- unique(unlist(sets, use.names = FALSE))
  if (length(ids) == 0) return(integer(length(all_combos)))

  member <- matrix(
    vapply(sets, function(s) ids %in% s, logical(length(ids))),
    nrow = length(ids)
  )
  key <- apply(member, 1, function(m) {
    paste(names(sets)[m], collapse = " & ")
  })

  as.integer(table(factor(key, levels = all_combos)))
}
```

## Pathway enrichment analysis

```{r enrichment-setup}
dirs <- c("Up", "Down", "Both")
dir_lab <- c(
  Up = "↑ Up-regulated",
  Down = "↓ Down-regulated",
  Both = "⇅ Both directions"
)

db_lab <- c(
  GO_BP = "GO: Biological process",
  GO_MF = "GO: Molecular function",
  GO_CC = "GO: Cellular component",
  KEGG = "KEGG",
  Reactome = "Reactome"
)
db_short <- c(
  GO_BP = "GO:BP",
  GO_MF = "GO:MF",
  GO_CC = "GO:CC",
  KEGG = "KEGG",
  Reactome = "Reactome"
)

# One part of every per-contrast Rds, as one table
bind_part <- function(part) bind_rows(lapply(enr, `[[`, part))

enr_cfg <- enr[[1]]$settings
enr_stats <- bind_part("stats")
enr_universe <- bind_part("universe")

# "GO" in --databases stands for its three ontologies
dbs <- names(db_lab)[sub("_.*$", "", names(db_lab)) %in% enr_cfg$databases]

# "7/37" -> 0.189, so fold enrichment = GeneRatio / BgRatio
ratio_num <- function(x) {
  vapply(
    strsplit(as.character(x), "/"),
    function(z) as.numeric(z[1]) / as.numeric(z[2]),
    numeric(1)
  )
}

terms <- bind_part("terms") |>
  mutate(
    contrast = factor(lvl_map[contrast], levels = contrasts),
    direction = factor(type, levels = dirs),
    database = factor(
      ifelse(database == "GO", paste0("GO_", ONTOLOGY), database),
      levels = names(db_lab)
    ),
    fold = ratio_num(GeneRatio) / ratio_num(BgRatio)
  )

# Number of groups each term is enriched in, per database and direction
any_season <- count(terms, database, direction, ID, name = "n_seasons")
all_seasons <- any_season[any_season$n_seasons == length(contrasts), ]

n_dir <- function(d, dir) sum(d$direction == dir)

# "12 (↑ 8 : ↓ 3)": both directions, then the up- and down-regulated tests
fmt_terms <- function(d) {
  paste0(
    comma(n_dir(d, "Both")),
    " (↑ ", comma(n_dir(d, "Up")),
    " : ↓ ", comma(n_dir(d, "Down")), ")"
  )
}

# Share of the background with an Entrez ID, over the groups
entrez_pct <- range(100 * enr_universe$entrez / enr_universe$genes)

# Enriched terms per group, both directions
n_terms_season <- vapply(contrasts, function(x) {
  sum(terms$contrast == x & terms$direction == "Both")
}, integer(1))
enr_text <- enum(sprintf(
  "%s in %s",
  comma(n_terms_season),
  group_lab[contrasts]
))
```

::: {.callout-note title="Method" collapse=true}

To investigate whether biological functions, processes or pathways were over-represented among the differentially expressed genes, we performed over-representation analysis (ORA) using the R-packages clusterProfiler (v`r enr_cfg$versions[["clusterProfiler"]]`; Wu et al., 2021) and ReactomePA (v`r enr_cfg$versions[["ReactomePA"]]`; Yu & He, 2016). Gene Ontology terms (biological process, molecular function and cellular component) were tested with the function "enrichGO", KEGG pathways with "enrichKEGG" and Reactome pathways with "enrichPathway"; the databases tested were `r enum(db_lab[dbs])`. ORA tests whether the gene list contains more members of a given gene set than expected by chance, using a one-sided hypergeometric test.

Each group was tested three times: with its up-regulated DEGs, its down-regulated DEGs and both directions together (padj < `r enr_cfg$gene_alpha`). Testing the directions separately is more sensitive, since a pathway whose genes change in both directions is diluted when they are tested together ([Hong et al., 2014](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsif.2013.0950)). The background (universe) was all genes in that group's DESeq2 results table, i.e. the genes that passed the gene filter, rather than the whole genome, which would favour terms whose genes are simply expressed in the tissue ([Timmons et al., 2015](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-015-0761-7)).

GO was tested with the Ensembl gene IDs; for KEGG and Reactome, the IDs were mapped to Entrez IDs with `r enr_cfg$orgdb` (v`r enr_cfg$versions[["orgdb"]]`), which `r sprintf("%.0f–%.0f", entrez_pct[1], entrez_pct[2])` % of the background had (@tbl-enrichment-sets). Gene sets of 10–500 genes were tested, clusterProfiler's default. P-values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg method, for GO over the three ontologies together, and terms with an adjusted p-value < `r enr_cfg$alpha` were considered significant. Terms supported by fewer than `r enr_cfg$min_count` genes from the input list were excluded.

```{r tbl-enrichment-sets}
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Genes in the enrichment tests per group. The direction columns show the DEGs (padj < ", enr_cfg$gene_alpha, ") that were tested. Background is all genes in the group's results table, and Entrez the number of those with an Entrez ID, which KEGG and Reactome are tested with.")

enr_stats |>
  distinct(contrast, type, genes) |>
  mutate(genes = comma(genes)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = genes) |>
  left_join(enr_universe, by = "contrast") |>
  mutate(contrast = factor(lvl_map[contrast], levels = contrasts)) |>
  arrange(contrast) |>
  mutate(
    contrast = unname(group_lab[as.character(contrast)]),
    across(c(genes, entrez), comma)
  ) |>
  select(contrast, genes, entrez, all_of(dirs)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Group", "Background", "Entrez", unname(dir_lab[dirs])
    ),
    align = "lrrrrr",
    row.names = FALSE
  )
```

:::

Testing both directions together, the number of enriched terms (padj < `r enr_cfg$alpha`) was `r enr_text`. Across the groups, `r comma(n_dir(any_season, "Both"))` terms were enriched in at least one group and `r comma(n_dir(all_seasons, "Both"))` in all `r length(contrasts)`. Testing the directions separately, `r comma(n_dir(any_season, "Up"))` terms were enriched among up-regulated and `r comma(n_dir(any_season, "Down"))` among down-regulated DEGs in at least one group, of which `r comma(n_dir(all_seasons, "Up"))` and `r comma(n_dir(all_seasons, "Down"))`, respectively, in all groups (@tbl-enrichment-counts).

```{r tbl-enrichment-counts}
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Enriched terms (padj < ", enr_cfg$alpha, ") per database and group. Each cell shows the terms enriched among the DEGs of both directions together, and in parentheses among the ↑ up- and ↓ down-regulated DEGs. The three are separate tests, so the up- and down-regulated terms do not add up to the first number. Any group counts each term once; All groups counts the terms enriched in every group.")
#| column: page-right

count_row <- function(db_sel, label) {
  per_group <- lapply(contrasts, function(x) {
    fmt_terms(terms[terms$database %in% db_sel & terms$contrast == x, ])
  })
  names(per_group) <- group_lab[contrasts]

  data.frame(
    Database = label,
    per_group,
    `Any group` = fmt_terms(any_season[any_season$database %in% db_sel, ]),
    `All groups` = fmt_terms(all_seasons[all_seasons$database %in% db_sel, ]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(dbs, function(db) count_row(db, db_lab[[db]]))),
  count_row(dbs, "**Total**")
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(contrasts) + 2)),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
```

### Shared between groups

The figures below compare the enriched terms across the groups, one tab per database. Each row is a term and each column a group, so a term enriched in every group has a point in every column; terms enriched in the most groups are at the top of each panel. The up- and down-regulated DEGs are shown in separate panels.

```{r enrichment-dotplot-functions}
# terms per group and direction in the dot plots
TOP_TERMS <- 5

wrap_text <- function(x, width = 55) {
  vapply(
    strwrap(x, width, simplify = FALSE),
    paste,
    character(1),
    collapse = "\n"
  )
}

# Top terms per group and direction, plus every other group they are
# enriched in; one row per term and group
dot_data <- function(db) {
  d <- terms[terms$database == db & terms$direction != "Both", ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(d)

  top <- d |>
    group_by(contrast, direction) |>
    slice_min(p.adjust, n = TOP_TERMS, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup() |>
    distinct(direction, ID)

  d <- d |>
    semi_join(top, by = c("direction", "ID")) |>
    group_by(direction, ID) |>
    mutate(n_groups = n(), best = min(p.adjust)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    arrange(direction, desc(n_groups), best) |>
    mutate(
      direction = droplevels(direction),
      row = paste(direction, ID, sep = "|")
    )

  # first term at the top of each panel
  d$row <- factor(d$row, levels = rev(unique(d$row)))
  d
}

dot_list <- lapply(setNames(names(db_lab), names(db_lab)), dot_data)

# Figure height from the number of label lines
fig_h <- vapply(dot_list, function(d) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(2)
  rows <- d[!duplicated(d$row), ]
  n_lines <- sum(lengths(strsplit(wrap_text(rows$Description), "\n")))
  max(3, 1.8 + 0.22 * n_lines)
}, numeric(1))

plot_dots <- function(db) {
  d <- dot_list[[db]]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    msg <- if (db %in% dbs) "No enriched terms" else "Not run"
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = msg, colour = "grey40") +
        theme_void()
    )
  }

  rows <- d[!duplicated(d$row), ]
  y_lab <- setNames(wrap_text(rows$Description), as.character(rows$row))

  ggplot(d, aes(contrast, row)) +
    geom_point(
      aes(size = fold, fill = -log10(p.adjust)),
      shape = 21,
      colour = "grey20",
      stroke = 0.3
    ) +
    facet_grid(
      direction ~ .,
      scales = "free_y",
      space = "free_y",
      labeller = as_labeller(dir_lab)
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = lab_fun, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = y_lab) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 7), name = "Fold\nenrichment") +
    # one-hue sequential ramp: light = least, dark = most significant
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low = "#b7d3f6",
      high = "#0d366b",
      name = expression(-log[10] ~ p.adj)
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_linedraw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

dot_cap <- function(db) {
  paste0(
    db_lab[[db]], " terms enriched among the up- (top) and down-regulated ",
    "(bottom) DEGs of each group, compared with ", ref, ". The ", TOP_TERMS,
    " terms with the smallest adjusted p-value per group and direction are ",
    "shown, together with every other group the term is enriched in. Point ",
    "size shows the fold enrichment (GeneRatio / BgRatio) and colour the ",
    "adjusted p-value; no point means the term is not enriched in that group."
  )
}
```

### Enriched terms per group

::: {.callout-tip title="Interactive table"}
The tables below have a drop-down menu which shows the genes included in the gene set, ranked by their shrunken log~2~ fold change. Click on the arrow ▶ on the left side of each row to reveal the genes. Gene names link to the corresponding [NCBI gene page](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/). The tooltip (appears when hovering) shows the log~2~ fold change of the gene in that group; red is up-regulated and blue down-regulated.
:::

```{r enrichment-table-functions}
# Shrunken log2 fold change per gene, for one group
lfc_lookup <- function(x) {
  r <- res[res$contrast == x, ]
  id <- sub("^(ENS[A-Z]*G[0-9]+)\\.[0-9]+$", "\\1", r$gene_id)
  setNames(r$log2fc_shrunk, id)
}

# Gene symbols as Ensembl links, coloured by direction, sorted by log2FC
gene_links <- function(ids, syms, lfc) {
  v <- unname(lfc[ids])

  tags <- lapply(order(v, decreasing = TRUE, na.last = TRUE), function(i) {
    tip <- if (is.na(v[i])) "log2FC: NA" else sprintf("log2FC: %+.2f", v[i])
    col <- if (is.na(v[i])) {
      "#555"
    } else if (v[i] > 0) {
      dir_colours[["Up"]]
    } else {
      dir_colours[["Down"]]
    }

    htmltools::a(
      syms[i],
      href = paste0("https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/?term=", ids[i]),
      target = "_blank",
      rel = "noopener",
      title = tip,
      style = sprintf("color:%s;", col)
    )
  })

  # interleave ", " between the link tags
  head(unlist(lapply(tags, list, ", "), recursive = FALSE), -1)
}

# dropdown filter over the databases
source_filter <- function(values, name, tbl_id) {
  js <- sprintf(
    "Reactable.setFilter('%s', '%s', event.target.value || undefined)",
    tbl_id,
    name
  )
  options <- lapply(sort(unique(values)), function(v) {
    htmltools::tags$option(value = v, v)
  })

  htmltools::tags$select(
    onchange = js,
    htmltools::tags$option(value = "", "All"),
    options,
    style = "width:100%; font-size:0.85em;"
  )
}

enrichment_table <- function(x, dir) {
  d <- terms[terms$contrast == x & terms$direction == dir, ]
  d <- d[order(d$database, d$p.adjust), ]
  d$source <- unname(db_short[as.character(d$database)])

  lfc <- lfc_lookup(x)
  tbl_id <- paste("enr", x, dir, sep = "-")
  cols <- c("source", "Description", "ID", "Count", "fold", "p.adjust")

  reactable(
    as.data.frame(d[, cols]),
    elementId = tbl_id,
    columns = list(
      source = colDef(
        name = "Source",
        maxWidth = 110,
        filterInput = function(values, name) {
          source_filter(values, name, tbl_id)
        }
      ),
      Description = colDef(name = "Term", minWidth = 220),
      ID = colDef(name = "Term ID", maxWidth = 150),
      Count = colDef(maxWidth = 70),
      fold = colDef(
        name = "Fold",
        maxWidth = 80,
        format = colFormat(digits = 1)
      ),
      p.adjust = colDef(
        name = "p.adj",
        maxWidth = 90,
        cell = function(value) signif(value, 3)
      )
    ),
    filterable = TRUE,
    defaultSorted = list(source = "asc", p.adjust = "asc"),
    details = function(index) {
      htmltools::div(
        style = "padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.8em;",
        htmltools::strong("Genes (sorted by shrunken log2 fold change): "),
        gene_links(d$gene_id[[index]], d$gene_name[[index]], lfc)
      )
    },
    defaultPageSize = 10,
    striped = TRUE,
    highlight = TRUE,
    compact = TRUE,
    theme = reactableTheme(cellPadding = "4px 6px")
  )
}

# one tabset per group: up, down and both directions
enrichment_tabs <- function(x) {
  n <- table(factor(
    as.character(terms$direction[terms$contrast == x]),
    levels = dirs
  ))

  cat("\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n")
  for (dir in dirs) {
    cat(sprintf("\n##### %s (%d)\n\n", dir_lab[[dir]], n[[dir]]))
    if (n[[dir]] == 0) {
      cat("_No enriched terms._\n")
    } else {
      print(htmltools::tagList(enrichment_table(x, dir)))
    }
    cat("\n")
  }
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

```{r pathway-enrichment-tables}
  cat("\n#### ", group_lab[[x]], "\n")
  enrichment_tabs(x)
}
```

### Genes behind the GO terms

The ORA tables and figures above look at the enriched terms one by one. This section turns the same results around and starts from the genes. Enriched terms often share most of their genes, also across the three ontologies, so several terms can be one signal counted more than once. Genes that are part of many enriched terms are the ones driving the GO results. Only the up- and down-regulated tests are used, so a gene counts once per group.

```{r gene-view-data}
# Databases in the gene view; add "KEGG" and "Reactome" to include them
GENE_VIEW_DBS <- c("GO_BP", "GO_MF", "GO_CC")

# genes in the kable, terms listed per gene in the lookup table, and terms
# and genes per heat map
GENE_VIEW_TOP <- 15
GENE_VIEW_MAX_TERMS <- 15
HEAT_TERMS <- 15
HEAT_GENES <- 40

# GO themes from go_themes.R when the report has them, NA otherwise; the
# ORA table `terms` itself is left as it is
gene_view_src <- if ("theme_id" %in% names(terms)) {
  terms
} else {
  mutate(terms, theme_id = NA_character_)
}
gene_view_themes <- any(!is.na(gene_view_src$theme_id))

# One row per gene and enriched term, from the up- and down-regulated tests
gene_long <- gene_view_src |>
  filter(
    as.character(database) %in% GENE_VIEW_DBS,
    direction %in% c("Up", "Down")
  ) |>
  select(
    contrast, direction, database, ID, Description, p.adjust, theme_id,
    gene_id, gene_name
  ) |>
  unnest(cols = c(gene_id, gene_name)) |>
  mutate(
    contrast = as.character(contrast),
    direction = as.character(direction),
    term_key = paste(database, ID)
  )

has_gene_view <- nrow(gene_long) > 0

# Shrunken log2 fold change per gene, one named vector per group
lfc_all <- lapply(setNames(contrasts, contrasts), lfc_lookup)

# One row per gene: enriched GO terms and themes over all groups
gene_summary <- gene_long |>
  group_by(gene_id) |>
  summarise(
    gene_name = first(gene_name),
    n_terms = n_distinct(term_key),
    n_themes = n_distinct(theme_id[!is.na(theme_id)]),
    n_groups = n_distinct(contrast),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n_terms), desc(n_groups))

# One row per gene and group: enriched GO terms, direction and log2FC
gene_group <- gene_long |>
  group_by(gene_id, contrast) |>
  summarise(
    n = n_distinct(term_key),
    dir = first(direction),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lfc = unname(mapply(
      function(g, x) unname(lfc_all[[x]][g]),
      gene_id,
      contrast
    ))
  )

# The terms of each gene as text: terms enriched in the most groups first,
# at most GENE_VIEW_MAX_TERMS
gene_terms_text <- gene_long |>
  group_by(gene_id, term_key, Description, database) |>
  summarise(
    n_groups = n_distinct(contrast),
    best = min(p.adjust),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(gene_id, desc(n_groups), best) |>
  mutate(
    lab = sprintf(
      "%s (%s)",
      Description,
      db_short[as.character(database)]
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(gene_id) |>
  summarise(
    terms = paste0(
      paste(head(lab, GENE_VIEW_MAX_TERMS), collapse = "; "),
      if (n() > GENE_VIEW_MAX_TERMS) {
        sprintf("; +%d more", n() - GENE_VIEW_MAX_TERMS)
      } else {
        ""
      }
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

gene_view_text <- if (has_gene_view) {
  top <- gene_summary[1, ]
  paste0(
    "In total, ", comma(nrow(gene_summary)), " genes were part of at least ",
    "one enriched GO term in at least one group. ",
    comma(sum(gene_summary$n_terms >= 10)), " genes were in 10 or more ",
    "terms, and the gene in the most terms was *", top$gene_name, "*, with ",
    top$n_terms, " terms in ", top$n_groups, " group",
    if (top$n_groups > 1) "s" else "", " (@tbl-gene-terms)."
  )
} else {
  "No GO term was enriched among the up- or down-regulated genes."
}
```

GO terms counts each term once, whichever group it is enriched in", if (gene_view_themes) ", and GO themes the themes those terms belong to" else "", ". The group columns show the number of enriched GO terms the gene is part of in that group, and whether the gene is ↑ up- or ↓ down-regulated there.")

```{r tbl-gene-terms}
  group_lab[names(tbl)[names(tbl) %in% contrasts]]
)

knitr::kable(

  align = paste0("ll", strrep("r", ncol(tbl) - 2)),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

One row per gene that is part of at least one enriched GO term. Type a gene name in the filter box of the Gene column to see every GO term it contributes to. The group columns show how many enriched GO terms the gene is part of in that group, with an arrow for its direction; the tooltip shows its shrunken log~2~ fold change. The last column lists the gene's terms, those enriched in the most groups first, at most `r GENE_VIEW_MAX_TERMS`.

```{r gene-lookup-table}
#| eval: !expr has_gene_view
#| column: page

lookup <- gene_summary |>
  left_join(gene_terms_text, by = "gene_id")

for (x in contrasts) {
  g <- gene_group[gene_group$contrast == x, ]
  i <- match(lookup$gene_id, g$gene_id)
  lookup[[paste0("n_", x)]] <- g$n[i]
  lookup[[paste0("d_", x)]] <- ifelse(g$dir[i] == "Up", "↑", "↓")
  lookup[[paste0("l_", x)]] <- round(g$lfc[i], 2)
}

# Gene symbol as a link to its NCBI gene page, built in the browser
gene_cell <- JS(
  "function(cellInfo) {
    return '<a href=\"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/?term=' +
      cellInfo.row['gene_id'] +
      '\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\"><i>' + cellInfo.value +
      '</i></a>';
  }"
)

# "12 ↑" in the colour of the direction, with log2FC as the tooltip
group_cell <- function(x) {
  JS(sprintf(
    "function(cellInfo) {
      if (cellInfo.value == null) return '';
      var d = cellInfo.row['d_%1$s'];
      var col = d === '↑' ? '%2$s' : '%3$s';
      return '<span style=\"color:' + col + ';\" title=\"log2FC: ' +
        cellInfo.row['l_%1$s'] + '\">' + cellInfo.value + ' ' + d +
        '</span>';
    }",
    x,
    dir_colours[["Up"]],
    dir_colours[["Down"]]
  ))
}

group_cols <- lapply(contrasts, function(x) {
  colDef(
    name = group_lab[[x]],
    cell = group_cell(x),

    maxWidth = 110,
    filterable = FALSE,
    sortNALast = TRUE
  )
})
names(group_cols) <- paste0("n_", contrasts)

hidden_cols <- c("gene_id", paste0("d_", contrasts), paste0("l_", contrasts))

names(hidden) <- hidden_cols

cols <- c(

reactable(
```

#### Genes × terms

The heat maps show, per group, the `r HEAT_TERMS` GO terms with the smallest adjusted p-value among the up- (top) and down-regulated (bottom) genes, and the `r HEAT_GENES` genes that are part of the most of these terms. A coloured cell means the gene is part of the term, coloured by its shrunken log~2~ fold change; an empty cell means it is not. Terms and genes are ordered by clustering on shared genes, so terms built from the same genes sit next to each other: a block of near-identical rows is one signal, however many terms it shows up in. The label ends with the term's `r if (gene_view_themes) "GO theme" else "ontology"`.

```{r gene-heatmap-functions}
#| eval: !expr has_gene_view

# Order of the rows of a 0/1 matrix by clustering on shared columns
cluster_order <- function(mat) {
  if (nrow(mat) < 3) return(rownames(mat))
  rownames(mat)[hclust(dist(mat, method = "binary"))$order]
}

# Gene × term table of one group and direction: the HEAT_TERMS terms with
# the smallest padj and the HEAT_GENES genes that are in the most of them
heat_data <- function(x, dir) {
  d <- gene_long[gene_long$contrast == x & gene_long$direction == dir, ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(d)

  top_terms <- d |>
    distinct(term_key, p.adjust) |>
    slice_min(p.adjust, n = HEAT_TERMS, with_ties = FALSE)
  d <- d[d$term_key %in% top_terms$term_key, ]

  lfc <- lfc_all[[x]]
  top_genes <- d |>
    count(gene_id, name = "n") |>
    mutate(abs_lfc = abs(unname(lfc[gene_id]))) |>
    arrange(desc(n), desc(abs_lfc)) |>
    head(HEAT_GENES)
  d <- d[d$gene_id %in% top_genes$gene_id, ]

  tag <- ifelse(
    is.na(d$theme_id),
    unname(db_short[as.character(d$database)]),
    d$theme_id
  )
  d$lfc <- unname(lfc[d$gene_id])
  d$term_lab <- paste0(wrap_text(d$Description, 45), "  [", tag, "]")

  # 1 where the gene is part of the term, 0 where not
  m <- 1 * (unclass(table(d$term_lab, d$gene_id)) > 0)
  d$term_lab <- factor(d$term_lab, levels = cluster_order(m))
  d$gene_id <- factor(d$gene_id, levels = cluster_order(t(m)))
  d
}

plot_heat <- function(d, dir, lim) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate(
          "text",
          x = 0,
          y = 0,
          label = "No enriched GO terms",
          colour = "grey40"
        ) +
        labs(title = dir_lab[[dir]]) +
        theme_void() +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
    )
  }

  gene_lab <- setNames(d$gene_name, as.character(d$gene_id))
  gene_lab <- gene_lab[!duplicated(names(gene_lab))]

  ggplot(d, aes(gene_id, term_lab, fill = lfc)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = gene_lab) +
    # diverging: blue down, grey 0, red up, symmetric around 0
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = dir_colours[["Down"]],
      mid = "#f2f2f2",
      high = dir_colours[["Up"]],
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-lim, lim),
      name = "Shrunken\nlog2FC"
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = dir_lab[[dir]]) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 90,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 0.5,
        face = "italic"
      ),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

# Up above Down, one colour scale for both
plot_heat_group <- function(x) {
  d_up <- heat_data(x, "Up")
  d_down <- heat_data(x, "Down")

  lim <- suppressWarnings(max(abs(c(d_up$lfc, d_down$lfc)), na.rm = TRUE))
  if (!is.finite(lim)) lim <- 1

  (plot_heat(d_up, "Up", lim) / plot_heat(d_down, "Down", lim)) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect")
}
```

```{r gene-heatmaps}

#| output: asis
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 12

for (x in contrasts) {
  cat("\n##### ", group_lab[[x]], "\n\n")
  p <- plot_heat_group(x)
  print(p)
  if (params$export_fig) {
    save_figure(p, name = paste0("fig-gene-heatmap-", x))
  }
  cat("\n")
}
cat("\n:::\n")
```

## Gene set enrichment analysis

```{r gsea-setup}
# Runs without GSEA results too, with empty tables, so that the inline code
# below still works; the section is then hidden
gsea_dirs <- c("Up", "Down")

# The HTML of every drop-down is built up front, so the tables keep the
# report small enough for Quarto with at most this many gene sets per
# database and table, and leading-edge genes per gene set. The TSV and Excel
# files of PATHWAY_ENRICHMENT_GSEA have every gene set and gene
GSEA_MAX_ROWS <- 100
GSEA_MAX_GENES <- 50

bind_gsea <- function(part) bind_rows(lapply(gsea, `[[`, part))

gsea_cfg <- if (has_gsea) {
  gsea[[1]]$settings
} else {
  list(
    databases = character(0),
    versions = c(clusterProfiler = "", ReactomePA = "", fgsea = "", orgdb = "")
  )
}

gsea_dbs <- names(db_lab)[
  sub("_.*$", "", names(db_lab)) %in% gsea_cfg$databases
]

rank_lab <- switch(
  gsea_cfg$rank_by %||% "",
  stat = "Wald statistic (`stat`)",
  log2FoldChange_shrunk = "apeglm-shrunken log~2~ fold change",
  log2FoldChange = "log~2~ fold change",
  paste0("`", gsea_cfg$rank_by, "` column")
)

empty_gsea_terms <- function() {
  d <- data.frame(
    contrast = character(0),
    direction = character(0),
    database = character(0),
    ONTOLOGY = character(0),
    ID = character(0),
    Description = character(0),
    setSize = integer(0),
    NES = numeric(0),
    p.adjust = numeric(0),
    Count = integer(0)
  )
  d$gene_name <- list()
  d$gene_id <- list()
  d
}

gsea_terms <- (if (has_gsea) bind_gsea("terms") else empty_gsea_terms()) |>
  mutate(
    contrast = factor(unname(lvl_map[contrast]), levels = contrasts),
    direction = factor(direction, levels = gsea_dirs),
    database = factor(
      ifelse(database == "GO", paste0("GO_", ONTOLOGY), database),
      levels = names(db_lab)
    )
  )

gsea_stats <- if (has_gsea) {
  bind_gsea("stats")
} else {
  data.frame(contrast = character(0), database = character(0))
}
gsea_universe <- if (has_gsea) {
  bind_gsea("universe")
} else {
  data.frame(contrast = character(0), genes = integer(0), entrez = integer(0))
}

# "12 (↑ 8 : ↓ 4)": gene sets, then those with a positive and a negative NES.
# A gene set enriched in opposite directions in two groups counts once in the
# total but in both arrows
fmt_gsea <- function(d) {
  paste0(
    comma(nrow(distinct(d, database, ID))),
    " (↑ ", comma(nrow(distinct(d[d$direction == "Up", ], database, ID))),
    " : ↓ ", comma(nrow(distinct(d[d$direction == "Down", ], database, ID))),
    ")"
  )
}

# Gene sets per group, any group, all groups in the same direction, and in
# opposite directions in different groups
n_gsea_group <- vapply(contrasts, function(x) {
  sum(gsea_terms$contrast == x, na.rm = TRUE)
}, integer(1))

gsea_text <- enum(sprintf(
  "%s in %s",
  comma(n_gsea_group),
  group_lab[contrasts]
))

gsea_any <- distinct(gsea_terms, database, ID, direction)
gsea_all <- gsea_terms |>
  count(database, ID, direction) |>
  filter(n == length(contrasts))
n_gsea_any <- nrow(distinct(gsea_any, database, ID))
n_gsea_opposite <- gsea_any |>
  count(database, ID) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  nrow()
```

```{r gsea-open}
#| output: asis

# The rest of the section sits in a div that is hidden without GSEA results
if (has_gsea) {
  cat("\n::: {.gsea-section}\n\n")
} else {
  cat(
    "_GSEA was not run: no `*_gsea.Rds` files in the enrichment folder",
    "(see `--enrichment_methods`)._\n\n::: {.hidden}\n\n"
  )
}
```

::: {.callout-note title="Method" collapse=true}

Over-representation analysis only uses the genes that pass the DEG threshold. To find gene sets whose genes shift together, also when few of them are significant on their own, we also performed gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA; [Subramanian et al., 2005](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0506580102)) with the clusterProfiler functions "gseGO" and "gseKEGG" and the ReactomePA function "gsePathway" (clusterProfiler v`r gsea_cfg$versions[["clusterProfiler"]]`, ReactomePA v`r gsea_cfg$versions[["ReactomePA"]]`), which use the fgsea algorithm (v`r gsea_cfg$versions[["fgsea"]]`; [Korotkevich et al., 2021](https://doi.org/10.1101/060012)); the databases tested were `r enum(db_lab[gsea_dbs])`.

GSEA uses no significance cutoff. All genes in a group's DESeq2 results table were ranked by the `r rank_lab`, and each gene set was tested for whether its genes are concentrated at the top or the bottom of the ranking. A positive normalised enrichment score (NES) means that the gene set is enriched among up-regulated genes, a negative NES among down-regulated genes, so each group was tested once, with both directions in one test. The leading-edge genes, the genes that drive the enrichment score, are listed for each gene set.

GO was tested with the Ensembl gene IDs; for KEGG and Reactome, the IDs were mapped to Entrez IDs with `r gsea_cfg$orgdb`, and when several genes mapped to the same Entrez ID, the gene with the largest absolute score was kept (@tbl-gsea-sets). Gene sets of `r gsea_cfg$min_size`–`r gsea_cfg$max_size` genes were tested. P-values were estimated with the adaptive multilevel method of fgsea, with a fixed random seed (`r gsea_cfg$seed`) so that reruns give the same result, and adjusted with the Benjamini–Hochberg method, for GO over the three ontologies together. Gene sets with an adjusted p-value < `r gsea_cfg$alpha` were considered significant.

```{r tbl-gsea-sets}
#| eval: !expr has_gsea
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Genes and gene sets in the GSEA per group. Ranked is the number of genes with a ", gsea_cfg$rank_by, " value, and Entrez the number of those with an Entrez ID, which KEGG and Reactome are tested with. The database columns show the gene sets tested (", gsea_cfg$min_size, "–", gsea_cfg$max_size, " genes); for GO, the three ontologies together.")

gsea_stats |>
  select(contrast, database, tested) |>
  mutate(tested = comma(tested)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = database, values_from = tested) |>
  left_join(gsea_universe, by = "contrast") |>
  mutate(contrast = factor(unname(lvl_map[contrast]), levels = contrasts)) |>
  arrange(contrast) |>
  mutate(
    contrast = unname(group_lab[as.character(contrast)]),
    across(c(genes, entrez), comma)
  ) |>
  select(contrast, genes, entrez, all_of(gsea_cfg$databases)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Group", "Ranked", "Entrez", gsea_cfg$databases),
    align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(gsea_cfg$databases) + 2)),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
```

:::

The number of enriched gene sets (padj < `r gsea_cfg$alpha`) was `r gsea_text`. Across the groups, `r comma(n_gsea_any)` gene sets were enriched in at least one group and `r comma(nrow(gsea_all))` in all `r length(contrasts)` in the same direction; `r comma(n_gsea_opposite)` were enriched in opposite directions in different groups (@tbl-gsea-counts).

```{r tbl-gsea-counts}
#| eval: !expr has_gsea
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Enriched gene sets (GSEA, padj < ", gsea_cfg$alpha, ") per database and group. Each cell shows the number of gene sets, and in parentheses those with a positive NES (↑, enriched among up-regulated genes) and a negative NES (↓, among down-regulated genes). Unlike the ORA counts, both directions come from one test, so within a group ↑ and ↓ add up to the first number. Any group counts each gene set once; a gene set enriched in opposite directions in two groups is counted under both arrows. All groups counts the gene sets enriched in every group in the same direction.")
#| column: page-right

gsea_count_row <- function(db_sel, label) {
  per_group <- lapply(contrasts, function(x) {
    fmt_gsea(
      gsea_terms[gsea_terms$database %in% db_sel & gsea_terms$contrast == x, ]
    )
  })
  names(per_group) <- group_lab[contrasts]

  data.frame(
    Database = label,
    per_group,
    `Any group` = fmt_gsea(gsea_any[gsea_any$database %in% db_sel, ]),
    `All groups` = fmt_gsea(gsea_all[gsea_all$database %in% db_sel, ]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

rbind(
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(gsea_dbs, function(db) gsea_count_row(db, db_lab[[db]]))
  ),
  gsea_count_row(gsea_dbs, "**Total**")
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(contrasts) + 2)),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
```

### Shared between groups

The figures below compare the enriched gene sets across the groups, one tab per database. Each row is a gene set and each column a group. Colour shows the NES, red for gene sets enriched among up-regulated and blue among down-regulated genes, so a gene set that changes direction between groups shows both colours in its row. Gene sets with the highest mean NES are at the top.

```{r gsea-dotplot-functions}
# Top gene sets per group and direction, plus every other group they are
# enriched in; one row per gene set and group
gsea_dot_data <- function(db) {
  d <- gsea_terms[gsea_terms$database %in% db, ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(d)

  top <- d |>
    group_by(contrast, direction) |>
    slice_min(p.adjust, n = TOP_TERMS, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup() |>
    distinct(ID)

  d <- d |>
    semi_join(top, by = "ID") |>
    group_by(ID) |>
    mutate(mean_nes = mean(NES)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    arrange(desc(mean_nes), p.adjust)

  # highest mean NES at the top
  d$ID <- factor(d$ID, levels = rev(unique(d$ID)))
  d
}

gsea_dot_list <- lapply(setNames(names(db_lab), names(db_lab)), gsea_dot_data)

# Figure height from the number of label lines
gsea_fig_h <- vapply(gsea_dot_list, function(d) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(2)
  rows <- d[!duplicated(d$ID), ]
  n_lines <- sum(lengths(strsplit(wrap_text(rows$Description), "\n")))
  max(3, 1.2 + 0.22 * n_lines)
}, numeric(1))

plot_gsea_dots <- function(db) {
  d <- gsea_dot_list[[db]]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    msg <- if (db %in% gsea_dbs) "No enriched gene sets" else "Not run"
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = msg, colour = "grey40") +
        theme_void()
    )
  }

  rows <- d[!duplicated(d$ID), ]
  y_lab <- setNames(wrap_text(rows$Description), as.character(rows$ID))
  nes_max <- max(abs(d$NES))

  ggplot(d, aes(contrast, ID)) +
    geom_point(
      aes(size = -log10(p.adjust), fill = NES),
      shape = 21,
      colour = "grey20",
      stroke = 0.3
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = lab_fun, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = y_lab) +
    scale_size_continuous(
      range = c(2, 7),
      name = expression(-log[10] ~ p.adj)
    ) +
    # diverging: blue = down, neutral grey at 0, red = up
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = dir_colours[["Down"]],
      mid = "#e6e6e3",
      high = dir_colours[["Up"]],
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-nes_max, nes_max),
      name = "NES"
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_linedraw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

gsea_dot_cap <- function(db) {
  paste0(
    db_lab[[db]], " gene sets enriched in the GSEA of each group, compared ",
    "with ", ref, ". The ", TOP_TERMS, " gene sets with the smallest ",
    "adjusted p-value per group and direction are shown, together with every ",
    "other group the gene set is enriched in. Colour shows the normalised ",
    "enrichment score (NES; red = enriched among up-regulated, blue = among ",
    "down-regulated genes) and point size the adjusted p-value; no point ",
    "means the gene set is not enriched in that group."
  )
}
```

### Enriched gene sets per group

::: {.callout-tip title="Interactive table"}
As for ORA, click on the arrow ▶ on the left side of a row to show the leading-edge genes of the gene set, ranked by their shrunken log~2~ fold change. Gene names link to the [NCBI gene page](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/), and the tooltip shows the log~2~ fold change of the gene in that group. Size is the number of genes in the gene set and Core the number of leading-edge genes. To keep the report small, each table shows at most `r GSEA_MAX_ROWS` gene sets per database, and each drop-down at most `r GSEA_MAX_GENES` leading-edge genes; the TSV and Excel files from PATHWAY_ENRICHMENT_GSEA have them all.
:::

```{r gsea-table-functions}
# The genes with the largest absolute log2 fold change, at most n
top_genes <- function(ids, lfc, n) {
  if (length(ids) <= n) return(seq_along(ids))
  head(order(abs(lfc[ids]), decreasing = TRUE, na.last = TRUE), n)
}

# Gene sets of one group and direction: the GSEA_MAX_ROWS with the smallest
# adjusted p-value per database
gsea_rows <- function(x, dir) {
  gsea_terms[gsea_terms$contrast == x & gsea_terms$direction == dir, ] |>
    group_by(database) |>
    slice_min(p.adjust, n = GSEA_MAX_ROWS, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup() |>
    arrange(database, p.adjust)
}

gsea_table <- function(x, dir) {
  d <- gsea_rows(x, dir)
  d$source <- unname(db_short[as.character(d$database)])

  lfc <- lfc_lookup(x)
  tbl_id <- paste("gsea", x, dir, sep = "-")
  cols <- c(
    "source", "Description", "ID", "setSize", "Count", "NES", "p.adjust"
  )

  reactable(
    as.data.frame(d[, cols]),
    elementId = tbl_id,
    columns = list(
      source = colDef(
        name = "Source",
        maxWidth = 110,
        filterInput = function(values, name) {
          source_filter(values, name, tbl_id)
        }
      ),
      Description = colDef(name = "Gene set", minWidth = 220),
      ID = colDef(name = "ID", maxWidth = 150),
      setSize = colDef(name = "Size", maxWidth = 70),
      Count = colDef(name = "Core", maxWidth = 70),
      NES = colDef(maxWidth = 80, format = colFormat(digits = 2)),
      p.adjust = colDef(
        name = "p.adj",
        maxWidth = 90,
        cell = function(value) signif(value, 3)
      )
    ),
    filterable = TRUE,
    defaultSorted = list(source = "asc", p.adjust = "asc"),
    details = function(index) {
      ids <- d$gene_id[[index]]
      keep <- top_genes(ids, lfc, GSEA_MAX_GENES)
      n_more <- length(ids) - length(keep)

      htmltools::div(
        style = "padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.8em;",
        htmltools::strong(
          if (n_more > 0) {
            sprintf(
              "Leading-edge genes, the %d of %d with the largest |log2FC| %s",
              length(keep),
              length(ids),
              "(sorted by shrunken log2 fold change): "
            )
          } else {
            "Leading-edge genes (sorted by shrunken log2 fold change): "
          }
        ),
        gene_links(ids[keep], d$gene_name[[index]][keep], lfc),
        if (n_more > 0) {
          htmltools::em(sprintf(
            " … and %d more, see the GSEA TSV for the full list",
            n_more
          ))
        }
      )
    },
    defaultPageSize = 10,
    striped = TRUE,
    highlight = TRUE,
    compact = TRUE,
    theme = reactableTheme(cellPadding = "4px 6px")
  )
}

# one tabset per group: positive and negative NES
gsea_tabs <- function(x) {
  n <- table(factor(
    as.character(gsea_terms$direction[gsea_terms$contrast == x]),
    levels = gsea_dirs
  ))

  cat("\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n")
  for (dir in gsea_dirs) {
    cat(sprintf("\n##### %s (%d)\n\n", dir_lab[[dir]], n[[dir]]))
    if (n[[dir]] == 0) {
      cat("_No enriched gene sets._\n")
    } else {
      shown <- nrow(gsea_rows(x, dir))
      if (shown < n[[dir]]) {
        cat(sprintf(
          paste0(
            "_Showing %s of %s gene sets: the %d with the smallest ",
            "adjusted p-value per database. All are in the GSEA TSV._\n\n"
          ),
          comma(shown),
          comma(n[[dir]]),
          GSEA_MAX_ROWS
        ))
      }
      print(htmltools::tagList(gsea_table(x, dir)))
    }
    cat("\n")
  }
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

```{r gsea-tables}
#| eval: !expr has_gsea
#| output: asis
#| column: page

for (x in contrasts) {
  cat("\n#### ", group_lab[[x]], "\n")
  gsea_tabs(x)
}
```
